subject.title: [Feature]: Add portable Agent Bundles for export/import across OpenClaw instances

question: Should portable agent bundles be a core `openclaw agents` export/import contract, a plugin/bundle-style contract, or deferred until a narrower plugin API exists?
rationale: The request crosses stable CLI/Gateway APIs plus security-sensitive config, auth, workspace, skills, bindings, and runtime-state boundaries, so automation should not choose the permanent product boundary.

options.title: Design a narrow bundle contract first
options.body: Define the non-secret manifest, dry-run, conflict/overwrite, skills/env checks, and core-vs-plugin boundary before any implementation PR.

options.title: Route through plugins or ClawHub
options.body: Treat portable agents as plugin/bundle distribution and only extend core where plugin APIs are missing.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Keep the existing manual agent, workspace, and plugin surfaces until there is a narrower deployment failure or stronger product demand.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow bundle contract first
recommendation.body: Define the non-secret manifest, dry-run, conflict/overwrite, skills/env checks, and core-vs-plugin boundary before any implementation PR.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work touches the agent CLI, add/auth-copy behavior, gateway agent file handling, and current docs surfaces most directly involved in a bundle contract decision.
